answer: Each identity locks a harbor bond; its work must clear a rising ledge. The harbor book counts every identity, each new one raising the ledge one point. A summit checkpoint admits only work at or above the ledge, scored by a public rubric anyone can re-score, and a summit recheck refuses below-ledge work. The first identity needs work worth 50 plus a 70 bond; the k-th needs 50+2(k-1) in work plus the same bond. A copied-score ring fails: copied work is deduplicated, scores zero, burns the bond. An honest agent pays 50 once and reclaims its 70 bond after a clean epoch; 1,000 fakes pay 1,119,000.
